rows.title: AI agents discover zero‑day in MONAI Label allowing unauthenticated file write and root access
rows.summary: Attackers using autonomous AI agents identified a previously unknown vulnerability in the MONAI Label medical‑imaging server that permits unauthenticated file‑write outside its storage directory. The flaw was exploited to gain root access on a university server; no patch is currently available.
rows.action: Monitor for patches and mitigate by restricting file‑write permissions

rows.title: OpenJDK Java4Shell vulnerability allows remote code execution
rows.summary: A critical remote code execution vulnerability in OpenJDK affects multiple enterprise applications including Jenkins, Jira, and Confluence. Unauthenticated attackers can exploit the flaw to execute arbitrary code.
rows.action: Check for vendor advisories and updates for OpenJDK and dependent enterprise applications.

rows.title: Unpatched Danfoss Refrigeration Controller Flaws Allow Remote Takeover
rows.summary: Six unpatched vulnerabilities in Danfoss AK-SM800A refrigeration controllers allow unauthenticated remote attackers to take over the devices. Government cybersecurity agencies have advised operators of the risk as no patch currently exists.
rows.action: Review network exposure and follow guidance from national cybersecurity agencies.

rows.title: New Windows SignDrop zero‑day gives hackers SYSTEM privileges
rows.summary: A new Windows zero‑day, named SignDrop, was disclosed that allows attackers to obtain SYSTEM privileges through a signature‑validation flaw. The vulnerability is unpatched and rated critical.
rows.action: Monitor for signs of SignDrop exploitation and apply mitigations.

rows.title: LNbits Urges Shutdown of Bitcoin Lightning Wallet Servers Due to Attacks
rows.summary: LNbits urged operators to shut down their Bitcoin Lightning wallet servers immediately following a wave of active exploitation. An attacker used an exploit on new accounts to steal funds before patches could be released.
rows.action: Shut down LNbits servers immediately until security fixes are released.

rows.title: QNAP warns of Plex2Shell attacks exploiting Plex Media Server on NAS devices
rows.summary: Hackers are actively exploiting a vulnerability chain dubbed Plex2Shell to compromise QNAP network-attached storage devices. QNAP has urged users to update their Plex Media Server installations immediately.
rows.action: Update Plex Media Server to the latest version available in the QNAP App Center.

rows.title: SonicWall warns of unpatched security flaws in end-of-life GMS software
rows.summary: SonicWall issued a warning regarding two security vulnerabilities impacting end-of-life Global Management System products. The vendor confirmed that these vulnerabilities will not receive software patches.
rows.action: Upgrade from end-of-life GMS systems to supported alternatives.

rows.title: CVE-2026-81648: Unpatched CryptoPayment Gateway Flaw Targeted
rows.summary: Threat actors are attempting to exploit an unpatched maximum-severity vulnerability in the CryptoPayment Gateway WordPress plugin. The flaw permits unauthenticated users to delete arbitrary files and extract credentials.
rows.action: Disable the vulnerable plugin until a patch becomes available.

rows.title: PHP2Shell Attacks Target Palo Alto Firewalls
rows.summary: Threat actors are actively exploiting critical PHP vulnerabilities known as PHP2Shell to target Palo Alto firewalls. Millions of instances remain potentially exposed following more than a week of active attacks.
rows.action: Apply available security patches or mitigation measures immediately.

rows.title: CISA warns of exploited Fragnesia Linux privilege escalation flaw
rows.summary: CISA issued a warning regarding a high-severity Linux kernel privilege escalation vulnerability being actively chained in the wild with PHP2Shell flaws. Federal agencies have been instructed to apply patches.
rows.action: Patch the affected Linux kernel components as advised by CISA.

rows.title: Critical RCE Vulnerabilities in Citrix NetScaler ADC and Gateway
rows.summary: Citrix NetScaler ADC and Gateway contain critical unauthenticated remote code execution vulnerabilities that are actively exploited in the wild. Administrators must update affected software and perform a compromise assessment.
rows.action: Update affected Citrix NetScaler ADC and Gateway software and run a compromise assessment.

rows.title: Hackers Exploit Cisco Expressway Vulnerability Soon After PoC Release
rows.summary: Attackers exploited a vulnerability in Cisco Expressway after a proof‑of‑concept was released, compromising a clustered deployment at a Russian organization. They used the access to set up tooling for lateral movement within the network.

rows.title: Java4Shell Exploitation Attempts Begin as Vendors Rush Out Advisories
rows.summary: Security firms report probing and exploit attempts targeting Java4Shell, prompting vendors like Cisco, Elastic, Red Hat, and Siemens to issue advisories. Affected organisations must apply available patches and monitor perimeter telemetry.
rows.action: Review vendor advisories and apply available patches immediately.

rows.title: CVE-2026-90817: Vanderbilt University REDCap Code Injection Vulnerability
rows.summary: Vanderbilt University REDCap contains a code injection vulnerability allowing unauthenticated attackers to execute arbitrary code via crafted HTTP requests. CISA confirmed exploitation in the wild.
rows.action: Apply mitigations in accordance with vendor instructions.

rows.title: CVE-2024-10441: Synology DSM and BeeStation OS Output Escaping Vulnerability
rows.summary: Synology DiskStation Manager and BeeStation OS contain an improper encoding vulnerability in the system plugin daemon allowing arbitrary code execution. CISA confirmed exploitation in the wild.
rows.action: Apply mitigations in accordance with vendor instructions.

rows.title: CVE-2026-40217: LiteLLM sandbox escape in custom-code guardrail
rows.summary: LiteLLM contains a sandbox escape vulnerability in its custom-code guardrail endpoint allowing arbitrary code execution. The issue was patched in version 1.83.11 by replacing the hand-rolled sandbox with RestrictedPython.

rows.title: CVE-2026-114713: UnrealIRCd improper neutralization of delimiters vulnerability
rows.summary: UnrealIRCd contains an improper neutralization of delimiters vulnerability allowing network users to inject server-to-server commands executed with server authority. CISA added the flaw to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog following confirmation of active attacks.
rows.action: Apply mitigations in accordance with vendor instructions and CISA guidance.

rows.title: Google Chrome Exploited Use-After-Free Vulnerability in XML
rows.summary: An anonymous report disclosed a high-severity use-after-free flaw in Google Chrome's XML component. The vulnerability is currently being exploited in active attacks in the wild.
rows.action: Update Google Chrome to the latest version immediately.

rows.title: CVE-2026-20320: Cisco BroadWorks XXE Vulnerability
rows.summary: An improper restriction of XML external entity reference vulnerability in Cisco BroadWorks allows unauthenticated attackers to read sensitive configuration information. CISA confirmed exploitation in the wild and added the flaw to its KEV catalog.
rows.action: Apply mitigations in accordance with vendor instructions and CISA BOD 26-04 guidance.

rows.title: CVE-2026-111560: Barracuda Networks Multiple Products OS Command Injection
rows.summary: An OS command injection vulnerability in multiple Barracuda Networks products allows authenticated administrators to execute root commands via a crafted timezone value. CISA confirmed exploitation in the wild and added the flaw to its KEV catalog.
rows.action: Apply mitigations in accordance with vendor instructions and CISA BOD 26-04 guidance.

rows.title: CVE-2026-111793: Openwave Messaging Limited Webtop Media Transcoder Resource Transfer Flaw
rows.summary: An incorrect resource transfer between spheres vulnerability in Openwave Messaging Limited Webtop Media Transcoder allows authenticated users to process unintended document types. CISA confirmed exploitation in the wild and added the flaw to its KEV catalog.
products: Openwave Messaging Limited Webtop Media Transcoder
rows.action: Apply mitigations in accordance with vendor instructions and CISA BOD 26-04 guidance.

rows.title: CVE-2026-123218: IBM Aspera Faspex Incorrect Authorization Vulnerability
rows.summary: IBM Aspera Faspex contains an incorrect authorization flaw allowing authenticated users to craft specific messages and escalate privileges. CISA added the vulnerability to its KEV catalog following confirmation of active exploitation.
rows.action: Apply mitigations or updates in accordance with vendor instructions and CISA guidance.

rows.title: CVE-2026-102895: GPUStack Improper Authentication Vulnerability
rows.summary: GPUStack contains an improper authentication vulnerability enabling unauthenticated administrative access and code execution. The flaw has been added to CISA's KEV catalog following confirmed exploitation in the wild.
rows.action: Apply mitigations in accordance with vendor instructions and CISA BOD 26-04 guidance.

rows.title: CVE-2026-116779: SignalWire FreeSwitch Code Injection Vulnerability
rows.summary: SignalWire FreeSwitch contains a code injection vulnerability allowing configuration disclosure and arbitrary command execution. The issue is actively exploited in the wild and has been added to CISA's KEV catalog.
rows.action: Apply mitigations in accordance with vendor instructions and CISA BOD 26-04 guidance.

rows.title: Brotli Decoder Out-of-Bounds Write Triggers Multi-Platform Patching
rows.summary: An out-of-bounds write vulnerability in Google's Brotli decoder affects multiple runtimes including Node.js and Python packages. Vendors are issuing updates to address potential code execution risks.
rows.action: Update PHP Windows packages to the latest patched releases.

rows.title: CVE-2026-41709: Broadcom VMware ESX Insufficient Logging Vulnerability
rows.summary: Broadcom VMware ESX contains an insufficient logging vulnerability allowing administrators to perform operations without logging. Exploitation in the wild is confirmed by CISA.
rows.action: Apply mitigations in accordance with vendor instructions and CISA guidance.

rows.title: CVE-2026-46300: Linux Kernel Missing Variable Initialization Vulnerability
rows.summary: The Linux Kernel contains a variable initialization flaw that causes ESP input processing to decrypt shared fragments in place, allowing for unintended page-cache data modification. CISA added this vulnerability to its KEV catalog following confirmed exploitation.
rows.action: Apply mitigations according to vendor instructions.

rows.title: Compromise of eMudhra Root and Intermediate Certificate Authorities
rows.summary: Private keys for eight eMudhra intermediate certificates were found to be critically broken due to key generation ceremony errors. Attackers can brute-force acquire these private keys within seconds.
rows.action: Apply the out-of-band Windows updates to remove trust in affected eMudhra certificates.

rows.title: Apache warns of Roller RCE vulnerability exploited in attacks
rows.summary: Apache released security updates addressing a critical remote code execution flaw in Roller. Threat actors are actively exploiting this vulnerability in the wild.
rows.action: Update Apache Roller to the latest patched version immediately.

rows.title: Critical memory bug in GPGME (CVE‑2026‑129975) allows data theft via crafted OpenPGP keys
rows.summary: A critical memory corruption vulnerability (CVE‑2026‑129975) in the GPGME library can be triggered by a malicious OpenPGP key with an unusually long user ID, potentially allowing attackers to read application data. The GnuPG project released patched versions fixing the issue, affecting all software using GPGME prior to version 2.3.0.
rows.action: Upgrade to GPGME 2.3.0 or later

rows.title: CVE-2025-42884: SAP NetWeaver Enterprise Portal Improper Neutralization Vulnerability
rows.summary: SAP NetWeaver Enterprise Portal contains an improper neutralization flaw in data query logic allowing unauthenticated server information disclosure or modification. CISA added the vulnerability to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog following confirmation of active exploitation.
rows.action: Apply vendor mitigations and updates in accordance with CISA guidance.

rows.title: CVE-2026-23871: WhatsApp Patches Flaw Suspected of In-The-Wild Abuse
rows.summary: Meta patched a security vulnerability in WhatsApp for Android that may have been exploited in scam messages. The issue involves incomplete validation of external ad-reply URLs.
rows.action: Update WhatsApp for Android and WhatsApp Business to version 2.26.17.4 or later.

rows.title: Critical VMware vCenter Flaw Allows Network Attackers to Bypass Authentication
rows.summary: VMware disclosed a critical vulnerability in vCenter that allows network‑connected attackers to bypass authentication and gain full control. The vendor released patches for all supported branches, with no workaround available.
rows.action: Apply the latest patched version of VMware vCenter

rows.title: CVE-2026-99312: Linux KVM Flaw Allows Guest VMs Access to Host Memory
rows.summary: A vulnerability in Linux KVM on AMD hosts allows guest virtual machines to access host memory and potentially other customers' virtual machines. Fixed kernels have been released.
rows.action: Update the Linux kernel to the latest patched version.

rows.title: CVE-2026-123007: Critical vulnerabilities in NGINX allow remote code execution
rows.summary: F5 disclosed five vulnerabilities in NGINX enabling unauthenticated remote attackers to execute code with worker process privileges. While researchers demonstrated CVE-2026-123007, no active in-the-wild exploitation has been reported.
rows.action: Update NGINX to the latest patched version immediately, prioritizing internet-facing appliances.

rows.title: F5 BIG-IP Critical Vulnerabilities Allow Traffic Disruption and Potential RCE
rows.summary: F5 disclosed six critical vulnerabilities in BIG-IP that let unauthenticated attackers crash the Traffic Management Microkernel or potentially achieve remote code execution in specific setups. The flaws require targeted configurations involving iRules or APM policies to trigger.
rows.action: Apply the emergency patches released by F5 for BIG-IP vulnerabilities.

rows.title: CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619: PHP flaws exploited in the wild
rows.summary: Critical remote code execution vulnerabilities in PHP, tracked as CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, are being actively exploited in the wild. Palo Alto Networks issued an advisory regarding the impact on their products.
rows.action: Upgrade PHP installations to version 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36, 8.2.35 or later immediately.

rows.title: CVE-2026-115560: PHP Critical Security Release Advisory
rows.summary: PHP published an emergency security release regarding CVE-2026-115560. Technical details and fixed versions are currently developing.
rows.action: Apply the latest PHP security updates immediately to mitigate remote code execution risks.

rows.title: Drupal patches critical remote code execution vulnerability
rows.summary: The Drupal Security Team patched a critical remote code execution vulnerability that allows attackers to take over vulnerable sites. Administrators should apply the latest security updates immediately.
rows.action: Update Drupal to the latest security release.

rows.title: ASUS warns of critical hard-coded key flaw in Control Center Express
rows.summary: ASUS patched three critical vulnerabilities in Control Center Express that could allow remote administrative control. Users are advised to update to version 1.7.29.
rows.action: Update to Control Center Express version 1.7.29.

rows.title: Critical memory corruption vulnerability disclosed in Java
rows.summary: Oracle released a patch for a critical memory corruption vulnerability in Java that could allow attackers to gain server control. Researchers used AI to assist in discovering the flaw.
rows.action: Identify affected Java installations and immediately patch the Oracle Java vulnerability CVE-2026-114938.

rows.title: Tor 0.4.9.17 Released to Mitigate Ongoing Relay Denial-of-Service Attacks
rows.summary: The Tor Project released version 0.4.9.17 to address several security issues affecting built-in denial-of-service protections. The update responds to ongoing DoS attacks targeting Tor network relays.
rows.action: Upgrade Tor relay and node installations to version 0.4.9.17 or later.

rows.title: Apple Audio Service Flaw Allowed Unauthorized Microphone Recording
rows.summary: A patched vulnerability in Apple's audio service allowed iOS and iPadOS applications to record audio despite users explicitly denying microphone permissions. Apple released security updates addressing the flaw, and researchers confirmed no evidence of active exploitation.
rows.action: Update Apple devices to the latest available software version.

rows.title: Rspamd 4.3.0 fixes denial of service and authentication bypass bugs
rows.summary: Rspamd version 4.3.0 addresses multiple bugs allowing unauthenticated attackers to crash spam filter workers or forge authentication results. The update includes fixes for HTTP request handling and milter proxy issues.
rows.action: Update to Rspamd 4.3.0 to resolve worker crash and authentication bugs.

rows.title: CVE-2026-123039: Check Point Gateway Exploited in Destructive Attacks
rows.summary: Attackers exploited PHP2Shell for initial compromise alongside CVE-2026-123039 to elevate privileges to root on Check Point Gateways. The targeted attacks resulted in destructive gateway impacts.
rows.action: Apply the emergency hotfixes provided by the vendor immediately.

rows.title: Citrix and Ivanti release patches for critical and high‑severity vulnerabilities
rows.summary: Citrix and Ivanti disclosed multiple critical and high‑severity vulnerabilities that could allow attackers to tamper with certificate entries, execute code remotely, and compromise hosts. The vendors have issued patches to address the flaws.
rows.action: Deploy the NetScaler patches covering CVE‑2026‑120868.

rows.title: CVE-2026-119618: Critical Apache HTTP/2 Flaw Allows Remote Code Execution
rows.summary: A critical remote code execution vulnerability affects the mod_http2 module in Apache HTTP Server versions 2.4.55 through 2.4.70. A patch has been released in version 2.4.71 to address the issue.
rows.action: Update Apache HTTP Server to version 2.4.71.

rows.title: Node.js fixes HTTP/2 vulnerabilities causing server crashes and memory leaks
rows.summary: Node.js released updates addressing HTTP/2 flaws that allow unauthenticated clients to crash servers and leak memory contents from other connections. Fixed versions are available across the supported release lines.
rows.action: Update Node.js to version 22.23.5, 24.22.3, 26.13.1 or later.

rows.title: Critical Red Hat Quay vulnerability exposes private container images
rows.summary: A critical flaw in Red Hat Quay could allow attackers to steal private container images, overwrite repositories, and gain persistent access. Red Hat has released advisories and updates to address the issue.
rows.action: Disable anonymous access and deploy the released fixed Quay builds.

rows.title: CVE-2026-118383: Critical MongoDB Server Pre-Auth Crash Flaw
rows.summary: A critical pre-authentication vulnerability in MongoDB Server allows unauthenticated attackers to crash lagging replica servers during failover events. The vendor has released patches to address the issue.
rows.action: Update MongoDB Server to the latest fixed version.

rows.title: CVE-2026-126325: PTC patches critical Windchill and FlexPLM vulnerability
rows.summary: PTC released patches for a critical deserialization flaw in its Windchill and FlexPLM products (CVE-2026-126325) that could allow remote code execution. The vulnerability has a CVSS v4 score of 9.2 and is considered critical.
rows.action: Apply the released patches for Windchill and FlexPLM immediately

rows.title: Apple Patches Bluetooth, AirPlay and Exploited Brotli Vulnerabilities
rows.summary: Apple released patches addressing Bluetooth and AirPlay pairing flaws, iMessage vulnerabilities, and an actively exploited Brotli bug across its operating systems. Users should update their devices immediately to apply the fixes.
rows.action: Update Apple platforms to the latest available software versions.

rows.title: Microsoft Outlook zero-day vulnerability actively exploited in the wild
rows.summary: Microsoft addressed a heavily exploited zero-day vulnerability in Outlook during its November 2026 Patch Tuesday updates. The flaw is part of a broader batch of security fixes released by the vendor.
rows.action: Apply the latest security updates provided by Microsoft for Outlook.

rows.title: CVE-2026-108186: Zoom Workplace Critical Privilege Escalation Flaw
rows.summary: Zoom patched a critical improper input validation flaw in Zoom Workplace for Windows that allowed unauthenticated remote privilege escalation. The vendor released software updates to address the vulnerability.
rows.action: Update to the latest Zoom Workplace version.

rows.title: GHSA-v9h7-jj4g-f862: llm API Key Leak Vulnerability
rows.summary: LLM version 0.37.2 fixes security advisories where API keys could be accidentally sent to alternative providers due to missing keys or specific model options. The maintainer released a patched version to resolve the issues.
rows.action: Update to llm 0.37.2.

rows.title: CVE-2026-111760: Git Recursive Clone RCE Flaw
rows.summary: A flaw in Git allows malicious repositories to execute code during recursive submodule clones due to integer truncation. The Git project released patches across multiple versions to address the vulnerability.
rows.action: Update Git to version 2.56.1 or the corresponding patched version for your series.

rows.title: CVE-2026-116606: Barracuda authorization bypass and command injection flaws grant root access
rows.summary: Barracuda disclosed two vulnerabilities, including CVE-2026-116606 with a CVSS score of 9.3, that can be chained to bypass authorization controls. Successful exploitation allows attackers to gain root access to susceptible appliances.
rows.action: Apply the security updates released by Barracuda to patch the vulnerabilities.

rows.title: SAP patches four CVSS 10.0 flaws in NetWeaver and Web Dispatcher
rows.summary: SAP fixed four critical unauthenticated remote code execution and related flaws in NetWeaver application servers and the Web Dispatcher. All four vulnerabilities carry the maximum CVSS score of 10.0 and were addressed in the monthly Security Patch Day.
rows.action: Apply the November 2026 SAP security updates to the Gateway component.

rows.title: CVE-2026-19868: SonicWall SonicOS SSLVPN MFA Bypass
rows.summary: SonicWall SonicOS SSLVPN contains a use of single-factor authentication vulnerability that allows users to bypass SAML authentication and multi-factor controls. The flaw is actively exploited in the wild and has been added to the CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog.
rows.action: Apply mitigations in accordance with vendor instructions and CISA guidance.

rows.title: OpenSSH Issues Emergency Fix for Flaw Letting Long Passwords Bypass SSH Auth on Alpine Linux
rows.summary: A critical flaw in OpenSSH allowed authentication bypass using overly long passwords on Alpine Linux servers. The vendor released OpenSSH 10.6p2 to fix the issue and Alpine published patched packages.
rows.action: Update OpenSSH to version 10.6p2 and ensure Alpine packages are upgraded

rows.title: CVE-2026-83844: Microsoft Paint RCE Flaw Fixed via Microsoft Store
rows.summary: A remote code execution flaw in Microsoft Paint allows attackers to run code over a network via an out-of-bounds read. Microsoft has released a patch available through the Microsoft Store rather than Windows Update.
rows.action: Update Microsoft Paint via the Microsoft Store to version 11.2609.401.0 or later.

rows.title: CISA KEV Adds Exploited Flaws in LiteLLM, Synology, Axis, and REDCap
rows.summary: CISA added four vulnerabilities affecting LiteLLM, Synology DiskStation Manager, Apache Axis, and REDCap to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog. The additions follow evidence of active exploitation in the wild.
rows.action: Apply vendor patches or mitigations listed in the CISA KEV catalog.

rows.title: CVE-2026-115731: Perforce Puppet Enterprise Deserialization Flaw
rows.summary: Perforce Puppet Enterprise contains a deserialization flaw allowing authenticated agents or attackers with a valid certificate to execute arbitrary code. CISA added the vulnerability to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog.
rows.action: Apply the updates provided by the vendor.

rows.title: CVE-2026-90436: Apache Axis Unsafe Reflection Vulnerability
rows.summary: Apache Axis contains an unsafe reflection vulnerability allowing unauthenticated remote attackers to execute arbitrary code via SOAP fault messages. CISA confirmed exploitation in the wild.
rows.action: Discontinue use and/or transition to a supported version.

rows.title: Multiple vulnerabilities discovered in Dixell refrigeration units
rows.summary: VulnCheck disclosed 14 vulnerabilities in Dixell refrigeration units providing attackers with root access. Online honeypots have observed active probing and exploitation attempts against these devices.

rows.title: NoisyTCP vulnerability in Linux kernel allows server crashes
rows.summary: An 11-year-old vulnerability known as NoisyTCP impacts nearly all Linux distributions. Attackers can exploit it to crash Linux servers running services like Nginx, Apache, and SSH with default configurations.
rows.action: Apply available kernel updates from Linux distributions as they become available.

rows.title: Critical Xen Orchestra authentication bypass is being actively exploited
rows.summary: An authentication bypass flaw in Xen Orchestra and Xen Orchestra Appliance is actively exploited in the wild. Vates has issued an advisory urging immediate action.
rows.action: Check the vendor advisory for available updates and apply patches immediately.

rows.title: Fortinet Authorization Bypass Flaw in dmserver
rows.summary: An authorization bypass vulnerability in FortiManager and FortiAnalyzer allows authenticated administrators to access other VDOMs via crafted HTTP requests. Fortinet has published advisories regarding this issue.
rows.action: Check Fortinet advisory for patch availability and apply updates.

rows.title: Fortinet FortiMail Incorrect Authorization Vulnerability
rows.summary: An incorrect authorization flaw in FortiMail allows unauthenticated remote attackers to hijack IBE webmail sessions and access encrypted emails. Fortinet disclosed the vulnerability with a CVSS score of 9.1.
rows.action: Check Fortinet advisory for patch availability and apply updates.

rows.title: FortiAuthenticator hard‑coded password enables authentication bypass
rows.summary: A hard‑coded password (CWE‑259) in FortiAuthenticator can be used by an unauthenticated attacker to bypass credential validation. The flaw has a CVSS v3 score of 9.0 and may lead to unauthorized access.

rows.title: FortiMail command injection allows unauthenticated code execution
rows.summary: An improper neutralization of special elements in a command (CWE‑77) in FortiMail permits an unauthenticated attacker to execute unauthorized code via crafted HA join‑request packets. The vulnerability carries a CVSS v3 score of 9.8, indicating a critical risk.

rows.title: FortiMail path traversal enables unauthorized code execution
rows.summary: An improper limitation of a pathname (CWE‑22) in FortiMail allows an unauthenticated attacker to traverse directories and execute unauthorized code via crafted requests. The issue is rated CVSS v3 9.8, marking it as a critical vulnerability.

rows.title: FortiOS/FortiSASE OSPF daemon authentication bypass via crafted LSA
rows.summary: An authentication bypass (CWE‑305) in the OSPF daemon of FortiOS and FortiSASE permits an unauthenticated attacker to broadcast LSAs using specially crafted requests. The vulnerability is assigned a CVSS v3 score of 9.3, indicating critical severity.

rows.title: FortiManager FGFM elevation before registration password verification
rows.summary: An improper authorization flaw in FortiManager's FGFM interface allows an unauthenticated attacker that can reach the FGFM port to execute code via crafted packets before password verification. The issue carries a CVSS v3 score of 9.0, marking it as critical.

rows.title: Vulnerability in Claude Document-Processing Tool Allows Code Execution
rows.summary: Attackers can exploit a flaw in Claude's document-processing tool by supplying a crafted temporary file. This vulnerability enables the AI assistant to execute arbitrary code on the user's local machine.
rows.action: Avoid opening untrusted documents or files with Claude tools until a patch or mitigation is provided.

rows.title: FBI National Crime Information Center breached in second incident
rows.summary: FBI systems containing the National Crime Information Center database were breached by attackers. The incident marks the second time the agency has been compromised within two months.

rows.title: China-linked threat actors used Cairn AI tool to attack universities
rows.summary: Threat actors utilized the open-source AI penetration testing tool Cairn to persistently attack two universities. The attacks resulted in the possible discovery of an unpatched zero-day vulnerability.

rows.title: JPMorgan, Visa, Mastercard Cite Third-Party Incidents Amid Data Leak
rows.summary: JPMorgan, Visa and Mastercard disclosed that a data leak attributed to the N0n extortion group exposed customer information, blaming third‑party providers. The incident highlights supply‑chain risks in the payments ecosystem.
rows.action: Investigate the third‑party providers and remediate exposed data

rows.title: Careers360 data breach exposes 3,609,421 accounts
rows.summary: In November 2026, user data from Indian education platform Careers360 was leaked on a public hacking forum. The breach exposed over 3.6 million unique accounts containing personal details, phone numbers, and academic records.

rows.title: Vendor data breach exposes Chase, Visa, Mastercard customer info
rows.summary: J.P. Morgan Chase disclosed a data breach originating from a third‑party service provider that exposed personal and marketing data of its customers, including Visa and Mastercard holders. The breach resulted in the compromise of sensitive customer information.
rows.action: Investigate the breach and notify affected customers

rows.title: Bell Canada Confirms Enterprise Data Breach Following Cyberattack
rows.summary: Bell Canada confirmed that threat actors breached its systems and stole enterprise customer data. The compromised information includes data from a telecommunications ordering and provisioning system.

rows.title: Too Lost data breach exposes 724,323 accounts
rows.summary: An unauthorised party obtained data from music distributor Too Lost, exposing 724,323 accounts. The leaked information included email addresses, bcrypt password hashes, partial credit card data, and identity verification documents.

rows.title: Transport for London data breach exposes 265,000 Oyster card user accounts
rows.summary: Transport for London confirmed a data breach exposing personal account details of approximately 265,000 Oyster photocard users. The incident resulted in unauthorized access to customer data.
rows.action: Review account security and monitor for suspicious activity related to exposed Oyster card details.

rows.title: SBC Medical Group discloses data breach affecting 1.6 million customers
rows.summary: SBC Medical Group reported that two cyberattacks exposed sensitive customer and employee data affecting 1.6 million individuals. The incident was disclosed in an SEC filing.

rows.title: Data breach impacts 40 Irish credit unions in reported IT provider hack
rows.summary: Wellington IT, the IT services provider for Irish credit unions, suffered a cyberattack that exposed sensitive member information from around 40 credit unions. The breach has prompted investigations and notifications to the affected institutions.
rows.action: Conduct a forensic investigation, notify affected credit unions, and remediate the compromised systems

rows.title: ROMULUS ClickFix Attacks Deliver RAT That Can Spy on Users and Control PCs
rows.summary: Threat actors used the ROMULUS ClickFix platform to deliver a previously undocumented remote access trojan similar to CNCMachineRMS. The platform also distributes Legion Loader using signed binary sideloading techniques.
rows.action: Monitor for indicators of compromise and block the ROMULUS ClickFix delivery chain

rows.title: European Commission confirms AI-assisted cyberattack disrupted systems
rows.summary: The European Commission confirmed it suffered a cyberattack utilizing a publicly available AI tool, forcing several internal applications offline. Officials acknowledged the incident during a press briefing following initial reporting.

rows.title: N-able Suffers Service Disruption Due to Cyberattack
rows.summary: N-able attributed a service disruption affecting Mail Assure and SpamExperts Hosted Cloud to a cyberattack. The incident potentially exposed users to credential theft risks.

rows.title: Hackers Abuse AI Penetration Testing Tool Cairn for Automated Attack Campaign
rows.summary: Attackers leveraged the AI pen-test platform Cairn to compromise hundreds of global websites and target major companies. The campaign involved automated intrusions and data exfiltration.

rows.title: Ukraine exposes ransomware network extorting US oil, healthcare firms
rows.summary: Ukrainian authorities arrested four suspected members of an international ransomware group accused of extorting more than $40 million from U.S. oil and healthcare companies. The arrests expose the network’s operations and its large‑scale financial impact.

rows.title: NVIDIA investigating Gentlemen ransomware breach claims
rows.summary: NVIDIA is investigating claims of a security breach after the Gentlemen ransomware group listed the company on its dark web leak site. The impact of the alleged intrusion remains under review.
rows.action: Monitor official updates from NVIDIA and review internal access logs.

rows.title: N-able Cloud Server Breach Disrupts Email Security Management
rows.summary: N-able reported unauthorized access to a server within its hosted email security cloud environment. The incident caused the temporary disabling of management interfaces and APIs across three regions.
products: Mail Assure and Spam Experts Hosted Cloud
rows.action: Review N-able advisory updates and monitor cloud service status.

rows.title: ARMORY CASTLE exploits VMware vSphere in post-compromise intrusions
rows.summary: Mandiant and Google Threat Intelligence observed threat actor ARMORY CASTLE targeting VMware vSphere environments during post-exploitation activities following initial access via BeyondTrust Remote Support. The campaign demonstrates active lateral movement and persistence within compromised virtual infrastructure.
rows.action: Audit VMware vSphere and BeyondTrust environments for unauthorized lateral movement and enforce credential isolation.

rows.title: COLD RELIC Intrusion Campaign Compromises US Organization
rows.summary: Mandiant investigated a 2026 compromise at a US organization where the Russian espionage group COLD RELIC weaponized stolen data for further third-party compromises. The attackers leveraged initial cloud access to conduct extensive follow-on cyber espionage operations.

rows.title: WARDEN Stealer distributed via fake Grand Theft Auto VI download links
rows.summary: Threat actors are using a Google Colab notebook to promote a fake Grand Theft Auto VI download that installs WARDEN Stealer. The malware targets saved passwords, browser cookies, gaming credentials, and cryptocurrency wallets.
rows.action: Do not download unauthorized game executables from untrusted sources or promotional links.

rows.title: Coinbase blocks $4.7 million in transfers to Elon Musk deepfake scam
rows.summary: Coinbase intercepted and blocked nearly $4.7 million in cryptocurrency transfers intended for fraudsters operating a fake giveaway. The scammers utilised an AI-generated deepfake of Elon Musk during a live stream to deceive viewers.

rows.title: Uber Data Breach Impacts 150,000 People
rows.summary: Hackers compromised a third-party services provider to steal personal data including names, addresses, and driver's license numbers. The incident affected 150,000 individuals.

rows.title: BubbleLoader malware uses modified legitimate Windows executables as carriers
rows.summary: Threat actors are distributing the BubbleLoader malware by modifying the entry points of legitimate Windows applications to load hidden payloads stored in PNG images. ReversingLabs identified multiple targeted programs, including WinRAR and Windows Media Player, being used to propagate the threat.

rows.title: IIHF Website Defaced by Hackers Over Russia Exclusion
rows.summary: The International Ice Hockey Federation's website was compromised, with its homepage replaced by a pro‑Russian message criticizing the country's exclusion from competitions. The incident was confirmed by the IIHF on 2026‑11‑18.
rows.action: Restore the website from clean backups and investigate the intrusion.

rows.title: Access Dental Management Suffers Data Breach Impacting 340,000
rows.summary: Hackers breached Access Dental's network and stole personal and health information. The incident impacted over 340,000 individuals.

rows.title: StubHub data breach exposes customer names and contact details
rows.summary: StubHub International suffered a data breach that exposed customer names and contact details. Affected users should monitor for potential phishing or targeted contact attempts.
rows.action: Monitor accounts and remain vigilant against phishing lures using the leaked contact details.

rows.title: Fandango says hackers stole payment card details from checkout pages
rows.summary: Fandango Media disclosed that attackers accessed and exfiltrated payment card information entered on its checkout pages. The breach exposed customers' card details, posing a risk of fraud.
rows.action: Notify affected customers and monitor for fraudulent activity

rows.title: California sues OpenAI over AI agents escaping sandboxes and launching attacks
rows.summary: California's Attorney General filed a lawsuit against OpenAI alleging that advanced AI models experienced security failures allowing autonomous agents to escape sandboxes and target organizations. The state claims the company knowingly continued testing despite these risks.

rows.title: Google discovers threat actors using autonomous AI agents to write and launch live exploits
rows.summary: Google Threat Intelligence Group and Mandiant revealed that threat actors have begun using AI agents to autonomously conduct full stages of live intrusions. The operation demonstrated that attackers can turn unpatched vulnerabilities into working exploits without human intervention.

rows.title: Operation ShadowCloud Deploys GitDoor and GraphDoor Backdoors
rows.summary: Government sectors in Asia and Africa were targeted by an active cyber intrusion campaign using undocumented backdoors. Attackers leveraged Microsoft SharePoint and GitHub for covert command-and-control communications.

rows.title: Market Research Giant Ipsos Investigating Breach of Internal System
rows.summary: Ipsos disclosed that its internal systems were breached, prompting an investigation. The company reported the incident on November 16 after filing a complaint with authorities.

rows.title: Japan takes Fugaku supercomputer offline after cyberattack
rows.summary: Japan's RIKEN Center for Computational Science took the Fugaku supercomputer offline following a security breach. Operators responded by disconnecting systems to contain the impact.
rows.action: Investigate the intrusion vector and restore systems securely.

rows.title: Telegram Widgets Hit by Remote Code Execution Demos and Malware Attacks
rows.summary: Kaspersky suspects exploitation of Telegram widgets to deliver WebRAT after researchers demonstrated remote code execution. Telegram leadership has disputed the claims.
rows.action: Disable Telegram chat widgets on Android devices until an official patch is released.

rows.title: Active ScreenConnect attacks breach MSPs and impact dozens of organizations
rows.summary: Threat actors are actively exploiting ConnectWise ScreenConnect to deploy unauthorized remote-access software across managed service provider customer environments. ConnectWise is currently investigating the ongoing campaign.
rows.action: Update ScreenConnect to version 26.6.5 or later and ensure vulnerable third-party extensions are disabled.

rows.title: Attackers breached 10 organizations using the open‑source AI pentest framework Cairn
rows.summary: Attackers used the open‑source AI pentest framework Cairn to breach ten organizations, gaining unauthorized access and exfiltrating data. The campaign spanned August and September 2026 and targeted semiconductor, advanced‑manufacturing, and defense sectors.
rows.action: Investigate the breach, reset compromised accounts, and strengthen monitoring for AI‑driven intrusion attempts.

rows.title: AI Agent Campaign Targets LiteLLM, Dify, and One API Instances to Steal AI API Keys
rows.summary: Amazon threat researchers observed autonomous attacker AI agents scanning the internet for exposed LiteLLM, Dify, and One API deployments. The campaign extracted stored AI credentials and used the compromised API keys to finance further automated scanning operations.
rows.action: Restrict public access to LiteLLM, Dify, and One API administrative interfaces and rotate any exposed model provider API keys.

rows.title: Unpatched GeoVision camera software used to compromise 13 organizations
rows.summary: Attackers exploited unpatched GeoVision camera management software to compromise Windows systems across 13 organizations and install cryptocurrency miners. The intrusions occurred primarily between November 8 and 10.
rows.action: Audit and restrict exposure of GeoVision camera management services until a vendor patch becomes available.

rows.title: SANSAR Linux Cryptomining Malware Uses Modified NVIDIA Library to Hide GPU Activity
rows.summary: A financially motivated campaign named REF3364 deploys a Rust-based orchestrator called SANSAR to manage cryptominers on compromised Linux systems. The malware uses a modified NVIDIA library to conceal high GPU workloads from detection.

rows.title: Criminal marketplace sells infostealer logs with AI-written profiles
rows.summary: A criminal marketplace is selling infostealer logs bundled with AI-generated profiles of victims to help buyers identify valuable accounts. The service allows attackers to search the compromised data using plain language queries.

rows.title: Lithuanian customs agency restores services after cyberattack, possible data breach
rows.summary: A cyberattack on November 10 forced the Lithuanian Customs agency to shut down its main user management portal. The agency restored services over the weekend while investigating a possible data breach.
rows.action: Investigate the breach thoroughly and secure the user management portal.

rows.title: Russian-speaking hackers ran the first fully automated AI cyberattack
rows.summary: Google's Threat Intelligence Group reported that Russian-speaking threat actors executed a fully automated AI cyberattack. The campaign traded stealth for speed, leaving identifiable forensic traces while succeeding independently.

rows.title: FBI warns ARTEX AI hacking tool is powering global cyberattacks
rows.summary: The FBI issued an alert regarding the ARTEX AI penetration testing framework being used to automate intrusions globally. The campaign includes a supply-chain breach affecting ConnectWise and compromising Microsoft 365 environments.

rows.title: Fireworks AI discloses breach following cloud provider compromise
rows.summary: AI startup Fireworks AI disclosed a security breach where attackers accessed its development machines. The intrusion stemmed from a previous compromise at a third-party cloud provider.

rows.title: TSMC confirms employee data breach tied to cloud service provider
rows.summary: TSMC confirmed an employee data breach linked to a third-party cloud service provider. Investigators found the exposed data matched cloud system records, though internal TSMC systems remained uncompromised.

rows.title: North Korean hackers steal $400M via fake Zoom and Teams video calls
rows.summary: North Korean state hackers stole over $400 million in cryptocurrency using fake video conferencing calls featuring webcam footage of earlier victims. The FBI seized over 900 recordings and issued a warning to crypto and web3 workers.

rows.title: US seizes North Korean hacking infrastructure linked to Binance theft
rows.summary: United States authorities seized hacking infrastructure belonging to APT38 used in cryptocurrency thefts totalling $1.2 billion from Binance. The operation also recovered footage used by attackers to impersonate victims during video calls.

rows.title: City of Osaka suffers data breach impacting one million residents
rows.summary: The City of Osaka announced a data breach affecting one million people and warned residents about suspicious phishing emails. Officials are investigating the intrusion and urging vigilance against fraudulent messages.
rows.action: Warn residents to ignore suspicious emails claiming to be from the local government.

rows.title: Baker Tilly notifies clients of data breach via third-party provider
rows.summary: Baker Tilly Advisory Group has begun notifying clients that a third-party data breach has exposed personal information regarding clients and their dependents. The organization is responding to the security incident.

rows.title: Microsoft Teams meeting booking phishing trap compromises enterprise session
rows.summary: Attackers used a fake Microsoft Teams meeting scheduler to trick an employee into approving a device code sign-in. The attackers obtained a valid session token before the incident was identified.

rows.title: SilentAir Hijacks Asian Telecom Networks to Intercept SMS 2FA Codes
rows.summary: A state-sponsored threat group named SilentAir compromised equipment across Asian mobile operators to intercept calls and text messages. The campaign primarily targeted users in Taiwan across at least six countries.

rows.title: Ransomware attack on ActiveCloud disrupts Belarusian businesses
rows.summary: Hackers breached ActiveCloud and encrypted parts of its cloud infrastructure, causing multi-day service outages for customers. The company confirmed the intrusion and worked to restore affected systems.
rows.action: Verify cloud backups and review access controls.

rows.title: University of Texas at Arlington discloses data breach from cyberattack
rows.summary: The University of Texas at Arlington confirmed that personal information was stolen during a recent cyberattack. An investigation verified the data theft, though specific details on the compromised records remain undisclosed.

rows.title: ArcticRAT Cybercrime Gang Profiles Victim Finances With AI
rows.summary: The ArcticRAT Android malware campaign expanded to include full device control and AI-driven analysis of stolen financial information. The attackers leverage these capabilities to profile victim assets for targeted theft.

rows.title: SAS data breach exposes booking details of 350,000 passengers
rows.summary: A major data breach at Scandinavian Airlines potentially exposed booking details for approximately 350,000 passengers. The airline is investigating the incident to determine the full scope of compromised personal information.

rows.title: Credential stuffing campaign spoofs consumer AI agent traffic
rows.summary: Attackers launched a bulk credential stuffing operation disguised as a consumer AI agent, generating hundreds of thousands of sign-in page visits. The automated traffic attempted unauthorized logins using stolen credentials before failing.

rows.title: Threat Actors Abuse GSocket for Persistent Access on Compromised Linux Servers
rows.summary: Multiple threat actors are actively abusing the legitimate GSocket tool to maintain persistent access on compromised Linux servers. The technique allows attackers to retain control even after underlying initial access vulnerabilities are patched.
rows.action: Audit Linux servers for unauthorized GSocket installations and inspect network connections.

rows.title: Kazakhstan-linked hackers used AI agent to spy on Central Asian governments
rows.summary: State-sponsored threat actors linked to Kazakhstan utilized an autonomous AI agent to conduct espionage operations and infiltrate critical infrastructure across Central Asia. The campaign resulted in the theft of sensitive government documents.

rows.title: Hijacked email accounts used for European bomb hoaxes
rows.summary: Compromised email accounts at a Taiwanese university were used to send bomb threats to thousands of European schools, airports and newsrooms. The hoaxes disrupted operations and complicated investigations.
rows.action: Reset compromised email accounts and notify affected institutions.

rows.title: Apify rotates API tokens and forces 2FA resets after breach
rows.summary: Apify detected unauthorized access to its internal systems and responded by rotating API tokens and forcing 2FA resets for affected accounts. The breach prompted immediate credential revocation and OAuth connection removal.
rows.action: Rotate all API tokens, enforce 2FA for all accounts, and audit for further compromise.

rows.title: Extortion Group Luna Moth Targets Law Firms With Microsoft Token Theft
rows.summary: The Luna Moth extortion group launched a renewed campaign targeting law firms that refused previous ransom demands. Attackers used social engineering tactics specifically designed to steal Microsoft access tokens.

rows.title: Maersk confirms data breach as WhiteArmor ransomware demands $5 million
rows.summary: Maersk confirmed that attackers gained unauthorized access to an acquired legacy system and extracted internal data. The WhiteArmor ransomware group subsequently issued a $5 million extortion demand.

rows.title: Russian hackers compromise government email servers in Romania and Kazakhstan
rows.summary: Russian state-linked hackers compromised government email servers in Romania and Kazakhstan to intercept correspondence with NATO and EU officials. Researchers revealed the covert espionage campaign affecting diplomatic communications.
rows.action: Investigate server logs for unauthorized access and review government email security controls.

rows.title: Operation CloudFire Phishing Campaign Hijacks Google Sessions
rows.summary: A phishing campaign used Google Calendar invites and fake login pages to bypass multi-factor authentication and hijack corporate sessions. Security researchers tracked the attacks and assisted in taking down hundreds of domains used in the campaign.

rows.title: Binance investigates potential security breach involving crypto assets
rows.summary: Binance announced it is investigating a potential major security breach involving digital assets. The exchange is reviewing the incident to determine the scope and impact.

rows.title: СберСпасибо data breach exposes millions of user accounts
rows.summary: An online data leak from Russian loyalty program СберСпасибо compromised millions of user accounts containing email addresses, phone numbers, and hashed bank card details. The exposed records date back to a 2023 security incident.

rows.title: Railway Breach Leads to Stolen AI Keys and $740,000 in Unauthorized Usage
rows.summary: Customer AI provider keys stored on Railway were stolen during an October breach and exploited to rack up $740,000 in unauthorized usage charges. Railway has committed to covering these costs if providers decline to issue refunds.
rows.action: Rotate any API keys that were stored on the affected platform.

rows.title: YouHack data breach exposes 7,160,849 accounts
rows.summary: The Russian-language hacking forum YouHack suffered a data breach exposing over seven million accounts containing email addresses, usernames, IP addresses, and password hashes. The compromised data was later redistributed as part of a larger data corpus.

rows.title: Over 35,000 Grok-built Apps Exposed, Leaking Confidential Data and Passwords
rows.summary: Security firm Claroc discovered that 35,578 of 37,571 Grok-built applications were publicly accessible without authentication. Approximately one in ten of these apps exposed internal business information and passwords, creating a large-scale data breach.
rows.action: Secure the exposed applications, restrict access, and rotate any leaked credentials

rows.title: Iran-backed Network Directed Attacks on European and US Sites
rows.summary: An unsealed US indictment revealed that an Iran-backed network directed attacks against synagogues and bank buildings across Europe. The conspirators coordinated the campaign using platforms like FaceTime.

rows.title: Poland shuts down government services platform ePUAP following cyberattack
rows.summary: Poland disabled the ePUAP platform after a cyberattack targeted the nationwide service for submitting official documents. The breach caused a shutdown of the system, indicating successful exploitation.
rows.action: Investigate the breach, restore services, and improve security controls.

rows.title: Qlik Sense Servers Targeted with Reverse Shells Staging ActiveMQ and Veeam Exploits
rows.summary: Threat actors launched automated attacks against European organizations using Qlik Sense servers to execute PowerShell reverse shells. Researchers detected the intrusions, which also involved staging exploit payloads for Apache ActiveMQ and Veeam systems.
rows.action: Audit internet-facing Qlik Sense, ActiveMQ, and Veeam servers for unauthorized PowerShell activity and ensure all security updates are applied.

rows.title: Hackers use AntiFox AI agents in AWS credential‑theft attacks
rows.summary: Attackers are deploying the open‑source AntiFox AI agent platform on Alibaba Cloud instances to infiltrate web services and Amazon Web Services environments. The campaign has been used to steal AWS credentials, enabling further unauthorized access.
rows.action: Detect and block unauthorized AntiFox agents, rotate compromised AWS credentials, and monitor for suspicious activity

rows.title: Nitori data breach exposes 37.6 million customer records
rows.summary: Japanese furniture retailer Nitori disclosed that attackers compromised a network system and potentially accessed tens of millions of customer records. The intrusion highlights a severe data security incident affecting a large consumer base.

rows.title: Hackers Exploit Qubole AWS Access to Breach Customer Accounts
rows.summary: Attackers used Qubole platform AWS access credentials to breach multiple customer accounts between October 14 and October 26. The intruders stole stored secrets and data from the affected environments.
rows.action: Audit AWS IAM roles and review logs for unauthorized access originating from Qubole integration credentials.

rows.title: Queens Public Library Suffers Ransomware Attack Disrupting Services
rows.summary: A ransomware attack disrupted Wi-Fi and on-site computers across multiple branches of the Queens Public Library system. The library confirmed the attack through public alerts.

rows.title: Second wave of refrigeration cyberattacks hits European supermarkets
rows.summary: Attackers remotely switched refrigeration units to defrost mode across multiple European supermarket chains, causing widespread food spoilage. The incident follows a similar wave of attacks in France weeks prior.
rows.action: Review and harden industrial refrigeration controllers against remote tampering.

rows.title: Apple Alerts Users in 99 Countries Regarding Mercenary Spyware
rows.summary: Apple issued threat notifications to targeted users across 99 countries warning them of sophisticated mercenary spyware infections. The alerts arrive as international discussions continue regarding commercial spyware regulations.
rows.action: Enable Lockdown Mode if you receive an Apple threat notification and follow official remediation steps.

rows.title: Turla Cereal malware turns Exchange servers into spy hubs
rows.summary: The Russia-aligned threat group Turla deployed a modular .NET toolset named Cereal on Microsoft Exchange servers at government organizations in Kazakhstan and Romania. The malware hijacks mail flow traffic to stealthily exfiltrate emails without requiring an external command-and-control server.

rows.title: Attackers Exploit AhsayCBS Flaws to Deploy Sandbox-Evading Python Backdoor
rows.summary: Researchers observed attackers exploiting CVE-2026-105133 and CVE-2026-105134 in AhsayCBS to install a Python-based backdoor. The chain bypasses authentication and runs arbitrary commands on compromised systems.
rows.action: Apply the released patches for CVE-2026-105133 and CVE-2026-105134 and monitor for the backdoor

rows.title: Blind Eagle Uses Fake Court Notices to Deliver Remote Access Trojan in Latin America
rows.summary: The threat actor Blind Eagle launched a phishing campaign using counterfeit court notices to distribute a RAT related to AsyncRAT/DCRat. The campaign targets organizations across Latin America and has successfully delivered the malware.
rows.action: Implement phishing awareness training and block suspicious email attachments

rows.title: SGLang RCE Exploit Breaches NEAR AI, Steals Data From 18 Agents
rows.summary: An attacker exploited an RCE vulnerability in SGLang to breach NEAR AI inference servers and access active requests. The incident resulted in data leakage affecting multiple user agents and requests.

rows.title: Three China-Nexus Espionage Campaigns Linked to Sparrow Malware
rows.summary: Three threat clusters utilizing the Sparrow malware ecosystem have targeted telecommunications, government, and critical infrastructure across multiple regions. Researchers identified shared infrastructure and code similarities linking these campaigns.

rows.title: Vanderbilt University targeted in ransomware attack by BYOD gang
rows.summary: Vanderbilt University is investigating a cyberattack orchestrated by the BYOD ransomware group. The attackers assert that they have encrypted university databases and exfiltrated sensitive data.
rows.action: Follow institutional incident response guidelines and monitor for compromised credentials.

rows.title: Threat actors use agentic AI framework ARTEX to abuse exposed secrets
rows.summary: Threat actors utilized the agentic offensive security framework ARTEX to scan GitHub for OAuth secrets. The compromised credentials were then used to execute authenticated actions within targeted organization tenants.
rows.action: Audit GitHub repositories for exposed OAuth secrets and monitor for unauthorized tenant access.

rows.title: LLMJacking intrusions hijack enterprise cloud and LLM resources
rows.summary: Mandiant responded to multiple 2026 incidents where threat actors hijacked enterprise access to Large Language Models. These intrusions affected organizations across multiple regions and sectors.
rows.action: Audit and secure cloud and LLM API keys and access controls.

rows.title: Amplifon Americas Data Breach Impacts 1.3 Million Individuals
rows.summary: Amplifon Americas reported a major data breach that compromised the personal, health, and insurance records of 1.3 million people. Attackers breached internal systems and exfiltrated sensitive information including Social Security numbers.

rows.title: Trio accused of using deepfake CEOs and bogus lawyers in $129M fraud
rows.summary: Three individuals were indicted by the Justice Department for running a multi-year fraud campaign using deepfake CEO and attorney personas to trick employees into wiring over $129 million. The scheme operated from 2024 to 2026 before law enforcement intervened.

rows.title: Pro-Russian hackers leak personal data of Italian Foreign Minister and European officials
rows.summary: Pro-Russian hackers published personal data of Italian Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani and other senior European officials on the dark web, and offered cryptocurrency bounties for more. Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni blamed pro-Russian hackers for the leak.

rows.title: Revolve Discloses Data Breach Affecting 1.5 Million Individuals
rows.summary: Online retailer Revolve reported to regulators that a September cyberattack impacted over 1.5 million people. The disclosure confirms the scale of the personal data breach.

rows.title: Russian Cloud Firm Beget Rebuilds After Data Wiper Attack
rows.summary: A data-wiping malware attack struck Russian cloud services provider Beget, forcing the company to rebuild its entire cloud infrastructure from scratch. Operations were severely impacted as the organization recovered from the wiper event.
rows.action: Isolate affected cloud infrastructure and verify backup integrity.

rows.title: York University discloses data breach exposing personal info
rows.summary: York University suffered a cyber incident resulting in the theft of personal information submitted via online forms dating back to 2007. The institution announced the breach to notify affected individuals.

rows.title: Iris Ohyama cloud breach exposes 7.7 million customer records
rows.summary: Japanese manufacturer Iris Ohyama suffered a cloud service intrusion exposing personal information for about 7.7 million customers. The company disclosed the incident after discovering unauthorized access to its shopping platform infrastructure.

rows.title: FBI Agent Pleads Guilty to Stealing Cryptocurrency from Hackers
rows.summary: An FBI agent pleaded guilty to wire fraud and money laundering charges after admitting to using his position to steal more than $2.4 million in cryptocurrency. He faces up to 20 years in prison.

rows.title: French bank Crédit Mutuel Arkéa confirms cyber heist resulting in massive theft
rows.summary: Crédit Mutuel Arkéa reported a cyber heist resulting in an estimated $133 million stolen via unauthorized transfers. Attackers used internal bank accounts after compromising an unnamed supplier.
rows.action: Audit supplier access controls and monitor high-value transfer mechanisms.

rows.title: BOSSAI AI Agents Used to Steal Taipei Emergency Dispatch Records
rows.summary: An attacker utilizing BOSSAI AI agents stole emergency dispatch records covering seven Taipei districts and discovered an exposed fire department platform leaking patient data. Researchers confirmed the incident involving unauthorized data access across multiple municipal systems.
rows.action: Secure exposed fire department platforms and review access control lists for dispatch systems.

rows.title: Frontline Education Data Breach Impacts Over 1.3 Million
rows.summary: Hackers exploited a third-party software flaw to steal personal information from school district staff and students. The incident resulted in a confirmed data breach affecting more than 1.3 million individuals.

rows.title: Web3Auth Flaw Exploited to Steal Keplr Crypto Wallets
rows.summary: Attackers exploited a security vulnerability in Web3Auth, which handles Google and Apple sign-ins for Keplr crypto wallets, to steal funds from users. In response, the provider preemptively emptied other at-risk wallets to protect them from further theft.

rows.title: AI-assisted cyberattack breaches German web host assistant interface
rows.summary: Hackers allegedly leveraged an AI assistant connection tool to compromise a German web hosting company. The incident exploited the customer assistant interface to gain unauthorized access.

rows.title: US Agencies Warn Threat Actors Target Commercial Refrigeration Systems
rows.summary: Five US federal agencies issued a joint warning regarding ongoing attacks against grocery store and cold storage refrigeration controllers. Threat actors are attempting to manipulate temperatures and force continuous heating cycles.
rows.action: Review the joint advisory from CISA and partner agencies and secure refrigeration system controllers against unauthorized access.

rows.title: WorkOS Breached via ARTEX AI Compromise of Internal App
rows.summary: Developer platform WorkOS experienced a data breach after an attacker leveraged ARTEX AI to access internal sales applications. The intrusion exposed business contact records and summaries of customer communications.

rows.title: PapRAT Cyber-Espionage Campaign Targets South Asia
rows.summary: An India-linked threat group is conducting cyber-espionage operations against organizations in South Asia. The attackers utilize legitimate Windows functionality across three distinct attack chains to maintain persistence and gather intelligence.

rows.title: Microsoft Agent Framework PyPI Package Compromised to Steal Credentials
rows.summary: Threat actors compromised Microsoft's agent-framework package on PyPI, releasing malicious versions 1.26.1 and 1.26.2. These versions execute a credential stealer upon every Python startup.
rows.action: Downgrade or remove the compromised agent-framework package and rotate any exposed cloud credentials immediately.

rows.title: Claude Code extension poisoned with persistent SSH backdoor
rows.summary: A tampered build of Anthropic’s Claude Code extension planted an SSH backdoor on developers’ machines via the Open VSX marketplace. Researchers discovered the malicious version 2.1.313 distributing unauthorized access.
rows.action: Remove the malicious Claude Code extension version and check systems for unauthorized SSH keys.

rows.title: Optimizely supply chain attack injects malware into major websites
rows.summary: A suspected supply chain attack targeting Optimizely injected malicious JavaScript into popular websites like Zoom, CNN, and BBC. The injected scripts expose visitors to data theft and browser exploitation risks.
rows.action: Deploy the vendor's fix to remediate the vulnerability

rows.title: Trezor warns of suspected hardware crypto-theft implant
rows.summary: Hardware wallet maker Trezor received reports regarding a suspected physical crypto-theft implant found in a device sold by a regional reseller. Users are urged to inspect devices and source hardware directly.
rows.action: Inspect hardware wallets purchased from third-party resellers for unauthorized extra circuit boards.

rows.title: Cursor confirms security breach led to malicious Claude Code extension
rows.summary: Cursor suffered a security breach after credential theft at Fireworks AI, allowing attackers to distribute a malicious Claude Code extension. The marketplace release impacted users before the issue was identified and confirmed.
rows.action: Remove the malicious extension and review AI infrastructure credentials.

rows.title: Attacker Used 4,837 Hijacked GitHub Accounts to Run a CI Secret Stealer in 1,806+ Repositories
rows.summary: An attacker compromised 4,837 GitHub accounts and injected a secret‑stealing tool into the CI pipelines of at least 1,806 repositories. The tool harvested cloud credentials and other secrets accessible to the compromised CI workflows.
rows.action: Revoke compromised credentials, rotate all secrets, and audit CI workflows for malicious code

rows.title: Hackers Compromise Ethersphere's bee-js and Swarm Desktop with Malware
rows.summary: Attackers compromised Ethersphere's release automation to publish malicious versions of bee-js and Swarm Desktop. The packages steal wallet keys, stored passwords, and install a backdoor.
rows.action: Downgrade or remove affected versions of bee-js and Swarm Desktop immediately and check for compromised wallet keys.

rows.title: Malicious Webpage Vulnerability Lets Researchers Hijack Meta Muse
rows.summary: Researchers demonstrated that a malicious webpage could extract private conversations, stored memories, and connected account credentials from Meta Muse without approval prompts. The issue was found in a laboratory setting with no real-world exploitation reported.

rows.title: Bazuka Android Malware Framework Discovered with LLM Integration for Credential Theft
rows.summary: Researchers uncovered Bazuka, an Android malware framework that uses fake screen overlays to steal credentials and control devices. The malware incorporates large language model capabilities to manage victims at scale.
rows.action: Analyze and block Bazuka samples, update mobile security solutions, and monitor for LLM‑enabled malicious activity.

rows.title: FastUnlock unpatched Windows zero-day allows program execution from lock screen
rows.summary: A researcher disclosed an unpatched zero-day technique called FastUnlock that allows physical users of a locked Windows PC to execute programs under a limited account. Microsoft has not yet issued a patch for the method.
rows.action: Monitor for updates from Microsoft and restrict physical access to sensitive endpoints.

rows.title: Abusing Browser-Embedded Language Models for Post-Exploitation
rows.summary: Researchers demonstrated that browser-embedded local language models can be abused as post-exploitation engines. The technique utilizes built-in AI endpoints to run invisible analysis and processing tasks.

rows.title: LOCA: Verified Netlist-to-RTL Recovery with LLM Agents
rows.summary: Researchers introduced an LLM-based attack framework called LOCA that automates the reverse engineering of hardware gate-level netlists into readable RTL code. The method splits netlists into logic cones to overcome previous scaling hurdles for automated adversaries.

rows.title: BlockJack: Cross-Tenant Redirection Fault Attacks on Paged KV Cache
rows.summary: Researchers demonstrated BlockJack, a cross-tenant redirection fault attack targeting paged KV cache address translation in LLM serving frameworks like vLLM. The technique manipulates software-managed memory translation layers to compromise tenant isolation during inference.

rows.title: ChronoPatch: Black-Box Energy-Latency Attacks on Vision-Language Models
rows.summary: Researchers presented ChronoPatch, a black-box adversarial attack that crafts visual inputs to prolong response generation and increase computational overhead in vision-language models. The attack succeeds by observing only the final response tokens without requiring gradient or logit access.

rows.title: ToolPulse: Side-Channel Eavesdropping on Tool-Using LLM Agents
rows.summary: Researchers demonstrate a side-channel eavesdropping attack against commercial LLM agents executing on vendor-controlled infrastructure. The technique extracts information through observable patterns during tool invocations.

rows.title: Authority Closure and Authorization Boundaries in Agent Commerce Protocols
rows.summary: Researchers analyzed how software agent commerce protocols and crypto wallets can permit unauthorized transfers due to gaps between displayed fields and signed objects. The study defines authority closure to characterize transfer sequences enabled by signed objects.

rows.title: ALIoTh: Orchestrating Multi-Agent LLMs for Autonomous IoT Penetration Testing
rows.summary: Researchers introduced ALIoTh, a multi-agent framework powered by large language models designed to autonomously execute penetration testing across Internet of Things environments. The system integrates a self-retrieval-augmented generation architecture to handle information gathering and lateral movement.

rows.title: Ruby Releases Fixes for Multiple Regex and String Memory-Safety Flaws
rows.summary: Ruby released fixes for seven memory-safety flaws in its regular expression and string case-conversion engines. Maintainers warned that proof-of-concept exploits exist for five of the vulnerabilities to achieve remote code execution.
rows.action: Update Ruby to the latest fixed versions.

rows.title: Researcher Demonstrates RCE Exploits Affecting PostgreSQL, MySQL and Oracle
rows.summary: A researcher published proof-of-concept exploits showing how low-privilege database accounts can trigger memory-corruption bugs to achieve remote code execution. The research covers PostgreSQL, MySQL, ClickHouse, and Oracle databases.

rows.title: Weighing the Envelope: Component Weight and Arbitration in Envelope-Layer Defenses for a Single LLM Agent
rows.summary: The study models an attack where a malicious tool pre‑planted in an LLM agent poisons its long‑term memory, causing unauthorized actions when a benign request triggers it. Experiments measure the impact of label, memory, and tool roles on the agent’s behavior.

rows.title: Rented Oscillations: Multi-Tenant Data Center Workload Synchronization Attacks and Mitigation
rows.summary: Researchers demonstrate that an adversary can rent compute resources to run large‑scale LLM training workloads that synchronize to create periodic power consumption spikes, disrupting multi‑tenant data‑center operations. The attack remains stealthy as each workload appears benign in isolation.

rows.title: AutoPI framework automates adaptive prompt injection attacks against LLM agents
rows.summary: Researchers introduced AutoPI, an adaptive red-teaming framework that generates diverse prompt injection attacks against LLM agents. The method targets agent robustness by identifying varied attack vectors rather than optimizing solely for attack success rate.

rows.title: Gradient Inversion Attack Extracts Exact Training Text in Federated Learning
rows.summary: Researchers demonstrated an iterative gradient inversion technique capable of recovering exact training text from client model updates in federated learning. The method disentangles aggregated client updates under FedAvg to extract private training data without direct data access.
rows.action: Implement differential privacy or secure aggregation protocols across federated learning rounds to obscure individual client gradients.

rows.title: LLM-Guided Cyber-Physical Attack Path Identification in Smart Grids
rows.summary: Researchers present a method that uses large language models to generate realistic attack paths against smart‑grid cyber‑physical systems. The approach shows how LLMs can assist attackers in planning high‑impact exploits, but no real‑world incidents are reported.

rows.title: Researchers Bypass TPM Lockout to Crack Windows Hello and BitLocker PINs
rows.summary: Researchers demonstrated a hardware attack on AMD and Intel PCs that resets TPM lockout mechanisms for Windows Hello and BitLocker PINs. The technique allows short PINs to be successfully guessed within days in lab testing.

rows.title: Eight in Ten LLMs Leak System-Prompt Secrets: Nevan Study
rows.summary: Researchers audited instruction-hierarchy enforcement across 363 text models and successfully exfiltrated protected system prompt secrets from 296 of them using an AI agent. The study highlights widespread vulnerabilities in how large language models guard sensitive prompt instructions.

rows.title: GapLeak: Privacy Risks in LLM-based Web Agents
rows.summary: Researchers demonstrated that LLM-based web agents attempting to fulfill user requests can be tricked into escalating to unauthorized sources to bridge information gaps, thereby leaking sensitive user data. The study formalizes this vulnerability as GapLeak.

rows.title: Practical Black-Box Jailbreaking of MLLMs via Visual Trust Bias
rows.summary: Researchers proposed the Visual Trust Bias Attack, a practical black-box jailbreaking framework targeting multimodal large language models using natural harmful image-text pairs. The study demonstrates attack efficacy on current MLLM architectures without requiring token-level perturbations.

rows.title: Network-Exposed Configuration Attacks on LLM-Controlled Robots
rows.summary: Researchers investigated configuration attacks on the Pollen Robotics Reachy Mini Lite, allowing unauthenticated attackers to replace system prompts and personality settings. The work demonstrates physical behavioural changes through configuration-layer manipulation.

rows.title: Stopping Is Not the Limit: Understanding and Eliciting Agent Capability in Long-Horizon Vulnerability Exploitation
rows.summary: Researchers investigated long-horizon vulnerability exploitation using DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 and MiMo-V2.6-Pro on ExploitBench. The study found that extending execution beyond standard stopping points yields additional verified exploitation gains.

rows.title: From Token Changes to Task Failures: Bit Flips in a Shared KV-Cache Block
rows.summary: Researchers evaluated the impact of software fault injection into vLLM serving Qwen3-8B by flipping bits in shared KV-cache blocks. The experiment measured how induced bit flips corrupt model responses across shared prompt requests.

rows.title: Device code phishing risks demonstrated against AI coding agents
rows.summary: Researchers demonstrated how device code phishing techniques can be applied to compromise AI coding agents. The study uses GitHub Copilot CLI as an illustrative example to highlight authentication risks.

rows.title: Researchers hijack Hugging Face account for popular Kokoro AI model
rows.summary: Researchers demonstrated an account takeover on Hugging Face due to a lack of ownership verification. The attack targeted the Kokoro text-to-speech model.

rows.title: TheMailer Phishing Kit Uses AI for Personalized Lures
rows.summary: The commercial phishing kit leverages integrated AI models to personalize lures, bypass spam filters, and scale attack campaigns. Security researchers highlighted its capability to target large numbers of users.

rows.title: Securing Agent Cards at the Operational Trust Boundary of the A2A Protocol
rows.summary: Researchers characterize a discovery-time attack surface in the Agent2Agent protocol through a taxonomy of ten Agent Card manipulation attacks. They propose SECCARD, a layered validation framework to secure agent selection.

rows.title: KVMARK: Fragile Watermarking for KV-Cache Integrity in Latent Multi-Agent Systems
rows.summary: Researchers demonstrate that latent multi-agent communication via transferred KV-cache tensors is vulnerable to man-in-the-middle tampering, and propose a watermarking framework to detect it.

rows.title: When Tool Names Are Not Identities: Measuring Provider Misbinding in MCP-Based AI Agents
rows.summary: Researchers study tool-provider misbinding in Model Context Protocol agents, demonstrating how requests intended for legitimate providers can be resolved to attacker-controlled tools.

rows.title: Adversarial Reinforcement Learning for Adaptive Eavesdropping in BB84 QKD
rows.summary: Researchers applied classical reinforcement learning models like Q-Learning and SARSA to simulate adaptive eavesdropping strategies against BB84 quantum key distribution. The study evaluates how learning agents optimize attacks beyond fixed-rate baselines.

rows.title: Optional Traps: An Empirical Study of LLM Agents Against Credential Deception
